title: Asymmetric cutover flow: canaryless passive->active promotion and backfill verification
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Summary: Design, implement, and validate an asymmetric cutover procedure for active-passive multi-region setups that avoids a canary phase (canaryless promotion) when the passive region must be promoted under severe capacity or network asymmetry. This ticket covers the runbook steps, automated verification harness for backfill/ledger reconciliation, circuit-breaker choreography, safeties for load shedding, and a scheduled drill plan with measurable SLO gates.

Goals: 
- Provide a deterministic promotion flow for passive->active in situations where a partial traffic canary is unsafe or increases surface area for inconsistency.
- Ensure data integrity: ledger/kv snapshot checksums, tokenstore validation, and sequence-aware backfill.
- Protect latency-sensitive clients by integrating circuit-breaker thresholds and staged load-shedding policies that respect SLO priorities.
- Make the flow automatable and observable so that DR drills can be executed with minimal human error and clear rollback criteria.

Scope: 
- Systems: serving runtime (request routing & KV cache), tokenstore, snapshot/backup storage, traffic router (gateway + edge), circuit-breaker service, autoscale controller, and the Console dashboards.
- Not in scope: full cold-start rehydration of archived datasets (>30d) and provider-level network restoration.

Success criteria (must pass for drill to be considered successful):
1) Promotion completes within target promotion window (90th perc promotion time < 7 minutes) without data loss.
2) KV and ledger snapshot checksums match post-promotion (byte-level) for 99.9% of active keys sampled.
3) No SLO regression > 5% in P99 latency for latency-sensitive routes during the steady-state 30 minutes after promotion.
4) Circuit-breaker engaged and load-shedding reduced traffic gracefully for non-critical routes (measured by drop rate and error budgets) rather than causing cascading failures.
5) Automated backfill job finishes without unresolved conflicts; any conflicts must produce deterministic reconciliation artifacts in /run/oncall/dr-backfill/*.log.

Planned runbook (high level):
1) Preconditions & preflight (automated): 
   - Run snapshot integrity check against last stable snapshot (sha256 checksums).
   - Verify tokenstore checkpoint sequence monotonicity.
   - Ensure passive region has required VPC connectivity to backup storage and control plane.
   - Validate autoscaler cooldowns and eviction thresholds are set to conservative values.
   - Emit a DR marker event to tracing (trace_id=dr-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>).
2) Quiesce non-critical routes: apply route tags and preemptively mark low-priority routes as drainable for 120s.
3) Freeze writes for margin window (if possible) and enable write-forwarding with sequencing tokens to backup (if writes cannot be frozen, enable sequence-aware append-only forwarder).
4) Promote passive region to active: flip routing at edge (atomic route rule swap with warmed route) and toggle circuit-breaker policy to permissive for critical routes, conservative for non-critical.
5) Warm caches: trigger targeted KV-cache prefetch for hot prefixes derived from telemetry.
6) Start deterministic backfill: run delta-applier job that replays append logs in sequence order with idempotency guards.
7) Validation & verification (automated): run checksum compare, tokenstore cursor reconciliation, sample-response diffing for golden prompts (structured checks in Console).
8) Observability sweep: validate SLOs for 30/60/120 minute buckets; surface anomalies to the DR channel and PagerDuty.
9) Postmortem signal capture: record all run outputs (snapshots, logs, metrics) to the DR forensic bucket and create a tilt report.
10) Rollback criteria: if checksum mismatch > threshold, persistent P99 latency regression, unresolved backfill conflicts after 60m — initiate rollback to previous region using staged snapshot snapback and circuit-breaker enforced in-flight reject for write paths.

Validation harness details: 
- "dr-verify" job (k8s cronjob invoked by runbook) performs: snapshot hash compare, tokenstore validation, sample request replay (10k curated prompts across priority tiers), and ledger gap detection.
- Conflict detector writes conflict artifacts with deterministic naming: dr-<run>-conflict-<seq>.json; these must be < 5 per 1M keys sampled to pass.
- Metrics: dr.promotion.duration_seconds, dr.backfill.conflicts, dr.kv.verify_match_rate, dr.slo.p99_ratio. Dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/dr/promotions (read-only link).

Circuit-breaker choreography: 
- Pre-promotion: lower circuit-breaker max-inflight for non-critical services to 25% of normal.
- During promotion: for critical services expand max-inflight by 10% temporarily while other services are intentionally limited.
- Post-promotion: stepwise restore using hysteresis windows tied to SLO buckets (restore when p99 stable for two consecutive 5-minute windows).

Load-shedding policy: 
- Define tiers: critical, degraded, best-effort. Pre-populate route labels and client tokens.
- Implement token-based shedding at the gateway to preferentially keep critical traffic.
- Add a synthetic request generator to maintain graceful load baseline for cold caches during validation.

Automation & PRs: 
- Runbook spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Asymmetric+Cutover+Runbook (draft)
- Implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8432 (runbook automation), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9009 (kv prefetch), https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/476 (circuit-breaker policy templating).

Drill plan: 
- Dry-run (tabletop) scheduled: 2026-03-08 (participants: Eng Oncall, SRE leads, PM, Solutions).
- Canaryless drill window: 2026-03-15 02:00-06:00 UTC (low customer impact timezone), with mandatory watch periods: prep (-24h), post (+6h).
- Failure simulation: partial network partition between primary and passive, and deliberate injection of increased latency to half of edge POPs to validate circuit-breaker behavior.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: deterministic backfill may hit non-idempotent side effects in integrations. Mitigation: run backfill in read-only stub mode against integrations and log diffs; only enable write-side effects after manual sign-off.
- Risk: SLO regressions causing customer-visible errors. Mitigation: aggressive preflight and ability to rollback within 15 minutes with route fencing and tokenstore snapshot swap.

Next steps: 
- Finish automation PRs and dependabot fixes (owners listed in PRs).
- Schedule tabletop and invite cross-functional stakeholders.
- Prepare drill telemetry live-run checklist and PagerDuty playbook.

Attachments & artifacts: 
- Draft runbook: confluence link above.
- Test dataset generator: gs://redwood-internal/dr-tests/asymmetric-cutover/
- DR forensic bucket for post-run artifacts: gs://redwood-forensic/dr-archives/
